description: Lamb Ouzi is a majestic Middle Eastern dish, featuring succulent, slow-roasted lamb infused with aromatic spices, typically served over a bed of fragrant rice. This celebratory meal brings together tender meat and savory grains, often adorned with toasted nuts, creating a truly unforgettable culinary experience. Its rich flavors and impressive presentation make it a centerpiece for any special occasion.

instructions.title: Prepare and Marinate the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb shoulder or leg dry. In a bowl, mix 2 tablespoons olive oil, minced garlic, chopped onion, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, seven spice, salt, and black pepper to create a paste. Rub this mixture generously all over the lamb. For best results, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow flavors to penetrate. If short on time, marinate for 30 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Sear the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). In a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy roasting pan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the marinated lamb on all sides until deeply browned and caramelized, about 5-7 minutes per side. This step builds a rich flavor crust.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Once seared, pour 2 cups of hot water or lamb broth into the bottom of the roasting pan. Cover the pan tightly with a lid or aluminum foil. Transfer to the preheated oven and slow roast for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until the lamb is fall-off-the-bone tender. The internal temperature should reach 90-95°C (195-205°F). Halfway through cooking, you may flip the lamb and check liquid levels, adding more if needed.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice
instructions.text: About 45 minutes before the lamb is done, drain the soaked basmati rice. In a large pot, melt butter or ghee over medium heat. Add diced carrots and cook for 3-5 minutes until slightly softened. Add the drained rice, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and bay leaf. Stir gently for 2 minutes to toast the rice slightly. Pour in 4.5 cups of lamb or vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Finish the Rice and Lamb
instructions.text: After 15 minutes, stir in the thawed frozen peas into the rice. Cover again and let it steam off the heat for another 10 minutes. Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Once the lamb is roasted, remove it from the oven and transfer it to a cutting board. Tent it loosely with foil and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This resting period allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in more tender and flavorful meat.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve the Lamb Ouzi
instructions.text: Carefully shred the tender lamb meat from the bone using two forks. Discard any bones or large pieces of fat. To serve, spread a generous bed of the aromatic ouzi rice on a large serving platter. Arrange the shredded lamb over the rice. Garnish generously with toasted pine nuts and slivered almonds. Serve immediately, perhaps with a side of yogurt sauce or a simple salad.

tips: For the most tender and flavorful lamb, marinate it overnight. The spices will penetrate deeper, resulting in a richer taste.
If bone-in lamb is unavailable, you can use a boneless lamb shoulder, adjusting cooking time slightly down. For a richer flavor, toast the rice slightly before adding broth.
Leftover Lamb Ouzi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of broth to the rice to prevent dryness. Serve with fresh mint tea.
article:
Mastering the art of Middle Eastern cuisine often involves a journey into rich flavors, aromatic spices, and time-honored cooking methods. Among the most revered and impressive dishes is Lamb Ouzi, a show-stopping centerpiece perfect for special occasions and family gatherings. Imagine succulent, fall-off-the-bone lamb, slow-roasted to perfection, served atop a fragrant bed of spiced basmati rice, adorned with toasted nuts. This isn't just a meal; it's an experience, a celebration of hospitality and culinary excellence.

Preparing Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi might seem daunting at first glance due to its grandeur, but the process is surprisingly straightforward, relying on patience and a few key techniques. The beauty of slow roasting is that it transforms a simple cut of lamb into an incredibly tender and flavorful masterpiece, infusing it with deep, savory notes that permeate every fiber. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create an unforgettable Middle Eastern dinner recipe that will leave your guests in awe.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi (also spelled "Qoozi" or "Ghoozi") is a quintessential Middle Eastern dish, particularly popular in the Levant and Gulf regions, often gracing tables at weddings, Eid celebrations, and large family feasts. At its heart, Ouzi consists of slow-cooked lamb, typically a whole leg or shoulder, though sometimes an entire lamb for grander events, served over a bed of highly aromatic rice. The rice itself is a star, often cooked with a medley of spices like cinnamon, cardamom, and allspice, along with ingredients such as toasted nuts (pine nuts, almonds, pistachios), peas, and sometimes even minced meat.

The hallmark of a truly authentic Lamb Ouzi is the incredible tenderness of the lamb, achieved through hours of slow roasting, which allows the meat to become so tender it practically melts in your mouth. The slow cooking also permits the spices in the rub to penetrate deeply, creating an explosion of flavor with every bite. It's a dish that embodies warmth, generosity, and the rich culinary heritage of the Middle East, making it an ideal choice for a memorable dinner recipe.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

To create this magnificent dish, you’ll need a selection of high-quality ingredients. The success of your Lamb Ouzi hinges on fresh components and aromatic spices.

**For the Lamb:**
*   **Whole Lamb Leg or Shoulder:** 4-6 lbs (bone-in is highly recommended for superior flavor and moisture).
*   **Olive Oil:** 1/4 cup
*   **Garlic:** 6-8 cloves, minced
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1/4 cup
*   **Salt:** 2 tablespoons
*   **Black Pepper:** 1 tablespoon
*   **Seven Spice (Baharat):** 2 tablespoons (a Middle Eastern blend, or make your own with equal parts ground allspice, black pepper, cinnamon, coriander, cloves, nutmeg, and cardamom)
*   **Ground Cinnamon:** 1 teaspoon
*   **Ground Cardamom:** 1 teaspoon
*   **Turmeric Powder:** 1 teaspoon
*   **Water or Chicken/Lamb Broth:** 2 cups (for the roasting pan)

**For the Ouzi Rice:**
*   **Basmati Rice:** 3 cups, rinsed thoroughly
*   **Olive Oil or Ghee:** 2 tablespoons
*   **Onion:** 1 large, finely chopped
*   **Garlic:** 3 cloves, minced
*   **Seven Spice (Baharat):** 1 tablespoon
*   **Ground Cinnamon:** 1/2 teaspoon
*   **Ground Cardamom:** 1/2 teaspoon
*   **Salt:** 1 teaspoon (or to taste)
*   **Black Pepper:** 1/2 teaspoon
*   **Chicken or Lamb Broth:** 5-6 cups (adjust according to rice package instructions)
*   **Frozen Peas:** 1 cup
*   **Optional:** 1/2 lb ground beef or lamb, browned and drained (for a richer rice)

**For Garnish:**
*   **Pine Nuts:** 1/2 cup, toasted
*   **Slivered Almonds:** 1/2 cup, toasted
*   **Fresh Parsley or Coriander:** 1/2 cup, chopped

## Step-by-Step Lamb Ouzi Recipe Instructions

Follow these steps to prepare your impressive Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:**
    *   Pat the lamb leg dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the surface of the lamb in a diamond pattern, making cuts about 1/2 inch deep. This helps the marinade penetrate and the fat render.
    *   In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, salt, black pepper, Seven Spice, cinnamon, cardamom, and turmeric to create a thick paste.
    *   Generously rub the spice paste all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scores. For best results, place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover it, and refrigerate to marinate for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight.

2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:**
    *   Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C).
    *   Place the marinated lamb in a sturdy roasting pan. Pour 2 cups of water or broth into the bottom of the pan (this helps create steam and keeps the lamb moist).
    *   Cover the roasting pan tightly with aluminum foil, ensuring no steam can escape.
    *   Roast for 3.5 to 5 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 190-200°F (88-93°C) and the meat is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb.
    *   For the last 30-45 minutes of cooking, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and develop a slightly crispy exterior.
    *   Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent it loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving or shredding. This resting period is crucial for juicy meat.

3.  **Prepare the Ouzi Rice:**
    *   While the lamb is resting, begin preparing the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil or ghee over medium heat.
    *   Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
    *   Stir in the Seven Spice, cinnamon, cardamom, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to toast the spices.
    *   Add the rinsed basmati rice to the pot and stir to coat it evenly with the spiced oil. If using, add the browned ground meat now.
    *   Pour in the chicken or lamb broth. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender.
    *   Remove the pot from the heat and let it sit, covered, for another 10 minutes.
    *   Stir in the frozen peas, then fluff the rice gently with a fork.

4.  **Assemble and Garnish:**
    *   Spread the fragrant Ouzi rice onto a large serving platter, forming a generous bed.
    *   Carve the slow-roasted lamb or pull it apart into large chunks and arrange it gracefully over the rice.
    *   Generously sprinkle the toasted pine nuts and slivered almonds over the lamb and rice.
    *   Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or coriander.

## Tips for Perfect Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

*   **Marination Time is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. The longer the lamb sits in the spice rub, the more flavorful and tender it will become. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Low and Slow:** The secret to truly tender, fall-off-the-bone lamb is low heat and long cooking. Resist the urge to crank up the oven temperature.
*   **Rest the Lamb:** This step is non-negotiable! Resting allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring it remains incredibly moist and tender.
*   **Don't Overcook the Rice:** Basmati rice cooks relatively quickly. Watch it carefully to ensure it's fluffy and separate, not mushy.
*   **Toasting Nuts:** Toasting the pine nuts and almonds in a dry pan or a little oil until golden brown enhances their flavor and adds a delightful crunch to the finished dish.
*   **Use Bone-In Lamb:** The bone adds significant flavor and moisture to the lamb as it cooks, resulting in a richer, more succulent final product.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a feast in itself, but it's traditionally served with an array of fresh and tangy accompaniments that complement its rich flavors.
*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple plain yogurt, or a more elaborate cucumber-mint yogurt sauce (like a mild tzatziki), provides a refreshing contrast.
*   **Fresh Salads:** Tabbouleh or Fattoush salad offer bright, herbaceous, and tangy notes that cut through the richness of the lamb.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles (like pickled turnips or cucumbers) add a wonderful sour crunch.
*   **Warm Pita Bread:** Perfect for scooping up any remaining rice or delicious lamb juices.
*   **Hot Sauce:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a side of your favorite Middle Eastern hot sauce can be a welcome addition.

## Variations & Substitutions for Ouzi

While the classic Lamb Ouzi is hard to beat, there are several ways to adapt this recipe to your preferences or what you have on hand.

*   **Different Cuts of Lamb:** While a whole leg or shoulder is traditional, you can use smaller cuts like lamb shanks, adjusting the cooking time accordingly. The slow-roasting method works beautifully for various lamb cuts.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** Feel free to tweak the spice blend for the lamb and rice. Add a pinch of dried lime (loomi) to the rice for a unique tangy depth, or a bay leaf for an earthy note.
*   **Rice Add-ins:** In addition to peas, consider adding golden raisins for a touch of sweetness, chickpeas for extra texture and protein, or even finely diced carrots to the rice. Some recipes include minced beef or lamb cooked into the rice for an even heartier dish.
*   **Pressure Cooker Lamb:** For a faster cooking time, the lamb can be cooked in a pressure cooker until tender, then finished in the oven for browning. While quicker, the deep flavor development of true slow roasting is often preferred for Lamb Ouzi.
*   **Vegetarian Ouzi:** While the focus here is lamb, the concept of richly spiced rice with nuts and vegetables can be adapted to a delicious vegetarian main by omitting the meat and focusing on roasted vegetables like eggplant, zucchini, and bell peppers.

Embark on this culinary adventure and bring the flavors of the Middle East to your table with this show-stopping Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi. It's a dish that promises not just a meal, but a memorable experience, deeply rooted in tradition and bursting with incredible taste.
